name: fix_express_command_injection
description: Fixes a command-injection vulnerability where user input is interpolated into a shell command string passed to child_process.exec
prompts: The Express server in server.js exposes GET /greet-cmd?name=..., which is supposed to respond with JSON {"output": "Hello, <name>"} by shelling out to the `echo` command. Right now it builds the shell command by directly interpolating the `name` query parameter into a string passed to child_process.exec, e.g. exec(`echo Hello, ${name}`, ...) - a classic command-injection vulnerability, since a value like `world; echo INJECTED` lets an attacker run arbitrary additional shell commands. Fix server.js so that arbitrary shell commands can no longer be injected via `name` (for example, by using child_process.execFile with the command and arguments passed as a separate array instead of a single interpolated shell string, or by strictly validating/sanitizing `name` to a safe character set and rejecting anything else with 400), while a normal name like 'Alice' still results in output containing 'Hello, Alice' with status 200. Keep listening on port 8028.
